# Zekke

> Zekke is a zero-knowledge encrypted vault for passwords, seed phrases, notes, long-form documents and, soon, files. Everything is encrypted in the browser before it is sent, with keys derived from a BIP39 recovery phrase that only the user holds. The recovery phrase is the account: there is no email, no password, and no account recovery of any kind.

Zekke is built by Zekke LLC (Sheridan, Wyoming, USA). The website is available in English, Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese.

## What it stores

- Secrets: seed phrases, account details, credentials
- Notes
- Long-form documents that sync across devices as you type, encrypted end to end; the server stores and forwards sealed changes and merges nothing
- Passwords
- Encrypted file storage (images and PDFs) and private sharing of one item with one person, planned for December 2026

## How it works

1. The browser generates a 12- or 24-word BIP39 recovery phrase and derives every key from it locally. Nothing is sent.
2. Every item gets its own random key, generated on the device and wrapped under a key derived from the phrase.
3. The server receives a sealed blob plus the little that routing needs: its size and when it changed. There is no master key, no recovery database and no support tool that can open a vault.
4. Typing the phrase into a new browser restores the whole vault. A 6-digit PIN locks the app on each device.

## Security model

- Zero-knowledge by construction, not by policy: Zekke cannot read user data, including under legal compulsion, because it never holds a key that could decrypt it.
- Losing the recovery phrase means losing the vault. Nobody, including Zekke, can restore access. Users verify their copy of the phrase at sign-up and receive a printable recovery kit.
- Standard mode: the PIN stays on the device; forgetting it only means signing in again with the phrase.
- Paranoid mode: the server also checks the PIN, so the phrase and the PIN together are required (two factors). Forgetting the PIN ends a Paranoid account.
- Post-quantum: data at rest uses AES-256-GCM, which survives quantum attacks. Sharing between accounts uses PQXDH, a hybrid of X25519 and ML-KEM-768, so an attacker must break both a classical and a post-quantum algorithm.

## Technical specifications

- Symmetric encryption: AES-256-GCM
- Classic key exchange: X25519 (ECDH)
- Post-quantum KEM: ML-KEM-768 (FIPS 203), for sharing
- Hybrid protocol: PQXDH (X25519 + ML-KEM-768), for sharing
- Key derivation: BIP39 → SLIP-0010 P-256
- Authentication: ECDSA P-256 signature over a fresh server challenge; no secret is transmitted
- PIN stretching: PBKDF2-SHA256, 600,000 iterations, client-side
- Server hashing: Argon2id (64 MiB, t=3, p=4)

## Business model and pricing

- No ads, no tracking, no cookies.
- A free tier; paid plans add storage. Final prices are not published yet.
- Waitlist members get 50% off premium subscriptions during the first month after launch.

## Release status

- September 2026: staging release, live now at https://test-app.Zekke.io. It includes the vault, encrypted notes and synced documents, in Standard and Paranoid mode.
- December 2026: the Drive (encrypted files) and private sharing.
- 2027: production launch; no date yet.
